why: The copy plan is right: it makes a new int array the same size as data2 and copies each element in order. But it writes data2.length() twice, and Java arrays have a length field, not a length() method, so the code does not compile. That makes it L2 with an error rather than correct new code.

concepts.quote: int[] copy = new int[data2.length()]; for (int i = 0; i < data2.length(); i++) copy[i] = data2[i];
concepts.why: It uses the right copy plan for data2 (new array first, then copy index by index), but data2.length() is a compile error.
Using new int[...] to make a separate array is right, but the size should be data2.length, not data2.length().
It uses int correctly for the index and the element type, but says nothing more about int.

concepts.quote: for (int i = 0; i < data2.length(); i++) copy[i] = data2[i];
concepts.why: The loop has the standard start, test and update for visiting every index 0..n-1, but the test calls length() on an array, which does not compile.
i++ is used correctly as the loop update, with no further reasoning about it.
It uses the primitive int correctly as the element type, and nothing more.
